$comment: Patches whose subject is control rather than sound. Nothing here makes a
noise on its own; the point is what happens to something else. The
recurring failure in this family is a modulator patched to a destination
that was never in the audio path, so the patch is correct and inaudible.

idioms.is: A slow oscillator modulating pitch by a small amount, so the note wavers around itself rather than moving to another note.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the pitch moves periodically and stays recognisably one note.

topology.describe: the modulator has to reach the oscillator's frequency input
the oscillator has to reach the audio path, or the vibrato is inaudible

common_mistakes.message: nothing modulates the pitch
the modulated oscillator is not in the audio path

idioms.is: A slow oscillator modulating an amplifier, so loudness moves periodically.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the level pulses at a steady rate.

topology.describe: the modulator has to reach the amplifier's control input
something has to pass through the amplifier to be tremoloed

common_mistakes.message: nothing modulates the amplifier
no audio passes through the amplifier

idioms.is: A modulator moving a filter's cutoff, so brightness changes over time.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the harmonic content changes audibly while the pitch does not.

topology.describe: something has to move the cutoff
audio has to pass through the filter

common_mistakes.message: nothing moves the cutoff, so the filter is static
no audio passes through the filter

idioms.is: An audio signal converted to a control voltage that tracks its loudness, then used to move something else.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the destination moves in step with how loud the source is.

topology.describe: audio has to reach the follower
the follower's voltage has to control something

common_mistakes.message: the follower has nothing to follow
the follower controls nothing

idioms.is: A modulation source passed through an attenuverter so its depth — and direction — can be set before it reaches its destination.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the modulation is present but clearly bounded.
idioms.source: Standard practice; the reason attenuverters exist

topology.describe: a modulation source has to reach the attenuverter
the scaled voltage has to reach a destination — attenuating a voltage nobody uses changes nothing

common_mistakes.message: the attenuverter's output goes nowhere
the attenuverter has no input

idioms.is: Two sources each modulating the other, so neither is simply the modulator — the pair produces behaviour neither has alone.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the result is unpredictable in a way that changes with either source's settings.

topology.describe: one source has to modulate the other
and the other has to modulate it back, or this is ordinary one-way modulation

common_mistakes.message: the modulation only goes one way

idioms.is: A stepped random voltage passed through a slew limiter, so it glides between values instead of jumping.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the destination drifts rather than stepping.
idioms.source: Standard practice; the difference between sampled and smooth random

topology.describe: the random voltage has to pass through the slew
the smoothed voltage has to control something

common_mistakes.message: the random voltage never reaches the slew, so it steps rather than drifts
the smoothed voltage controls nothing

idioms.is: A trigger-driven envelope closing an amplifier on a different signal, so one part steps aside for another.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the ducked part dips in time with the trigger and recovers.

topology.describe: something has to trigger the duck
the envelope has to control the amplifier being ducked
the ducked signal has to pass through that amplifier

common_mistakes.message: nothing triggers the duck
the envelope does not control an amplifier
no audio passes through the ducked amplifier

idioms.is: One modulator moving another's rate or depth, so the modulation itself is never constant.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the sense of motion changes over time rather than staying periodic.
idioms.source: Strange; the standard way to defeat obvious periodicity

topology.describe: one modulator has to move the other's rate
the modulated modulator has to control something

common_mistakes.message: no modulator moves another, so the motion is perfectly periodic
the modulation reaches no destination

idioms.is: Two signals through amplifiers under opposing control, so a voltage moves the balance between them.
idioms.sounds_right_when: one source gives way to the other continuously rather than switching.

topology.describe: a voltage has to control the balance
the two paths have to be summed

common_mistakes.message: nothing controls the balance
the two paths are never summed
